findings.location: M2, B07-TRUST-OPEN-CERTAIN, B07-TRUST-OPEN-UNCERTAIN, B06-TRUST-OPEN-6498 (basis and lead_kind trust_period_running_on_1934_06_18_continued_by_statute)
findings.claim: For every trust member whose period was running on 1934-06-18, IRA sec. 2 "extended and continued" the period the order fixed, so the stated end is not a sound TERM end; tribes outside the IRA are covered by M3 (the 1935 Act and later blanket orders).
findings.evidence: IRA sec. 13 (48 Stat. 986-987, read on govinfo STATUTE-48-Pg984.pdf) provides that sections 2, 4, 7, 16, 17 and 18 "shall not apply" to the listed tribes and affiliated tribes located in Oklahoma (Cheyenne, Arapaho, Apache, Comanche, Kiowa, Caddo, Delaware, Wichita, Osage, Kaw, Otoe, Tonkawa, Pawnee, Ponca, Shawnee, Ottawa, Quapaw, Seneca, Wyandotte, Iowa, Sac and Fox, Kickapoo, Pottawatomi, Cherokee, Chickasaw, Choctaw, Creek, Seminole). The member texts or WPA summaries put 19 open trust members in Oklahoma: EO 2317 (Eastern Shawnee), 3363 (Ponca, Okla.), 4029 (Mexican Kickapoo), 4281 (Otoe), 4384 (Eastern Shawnee), 4398 (Kiowa, Comanche, Apache, Wichita), 4435 (Iowa, Sac and Fox), 4470 (Modoc of Oklahoma; within the 'affiliated' clause only if affiliated, to be confirmed), 4557 (Absentee Shawnee, Citizen Potawatomi), 4587 (Cheyenne and Arapaho), 4588 (Ottawa, Seneca, Wyandotte), 4816 (Oakland reservation, Tonkawa), 4898 (Pawnee), 5306 (Seneca), 5539 (Ponca), 5728 (Otoe and Missouria), 5955 (Wichita), 6926 (all Oklahoma reservations), 7206 (all Oklahoma lands); EO 6498 also reaches Oklahoma lands. For these, sec. 2 continued nothing, so the stated basis is contrary to the statute the doctrine cites. M3 does not cover them either: the Act of June 15, 1935, sec. 3 (49 Stat. 378) reaches only reservations that voted to exclude themselves under sec. 18, which sec. 13 also makes inapplicable to these tribes. The doctrine itself notes (Other points) that EO 3363 is the Ponca (Oklahoma) period. The gap line "whether the tribe came under the IRA: the sec. 13 list" treats as unknown a fact the held texts already show.
findings.fix: Add a branch before B07-TRUST-OPEN for sec. 13 Oklahoma members (text/summary 'Oklahoma|Okla' plus the trust condition), with a basis stating that IRA sec. 2 does not reach them. By the doctrine's own M1 reasoning their stated periods (ending 1934-1946) are TERM ends unless a statute continuing those periods is found; either lead them `no`, TERM, interval = stated end, with the gap 'no later Oklahoma statute continuing these periods is held', or keep them `open` with that gap as the reason. Do not cite IRA sec. 2 continuation for them; correct M2 ('for tribes outside the IRA, M3 applies') to distinguish sec. 13 tribes from sec. 18 exclusions.

findings.claim: Each of these orders "fixed a trust period that was still running (or may have been running) on 1934-06-18" and IRA sec. 2 continued the period the order fixed.
findings.evidence: These orders were issued between 1934-12-20 and 1936-09-30, after the IRA. IRA sec. 2 continued "the existing periods of trust" on 1934-06-18; the extension each of these orders grants did not exist then, so sec. 2 cannot have continued it (for an IRA reservation sec. 2 had already continued the prior period indefinitely; the White Earth Act sec. 3(i), 100 Stat. 62, read on govinfo, likewise describes the IRA as extending indefinitely periods that would otherwise have expired on or after 1934-06-18). Four of the orders say so in their own terms: EO 6939 (Spokane) 'shall be subject to the provisions of the act of June 18, 1934 ... and if the provisions of said Act are made applicable to the said Reservation by the election provided for in said Act, this order shall thereafter cease to be of force and effect'; EO 6961 (Klamath), 6962 (Colville) and 7001 (Crow) contain the same cessation clause tied to a favourable sec. 18 vote (held texts in jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts/). The doctrine never mentions this own-terms end. For a reservation that rejected the IRA, the order's own period ran to 1945 (EO 7464: 1961-12-31 to 1962-12-31); EO 6926 and 7206 are Oklahoma orders (see R3). So in each alternative the order's own terms end it before the cutoff unless a reservation-specific statute continued that period (the 25 CFR ch. I appendix lists, e.g., an Act of Dec. 24, 1942, 56 Stat. 1081, for Klamath and a 1940 Act for Crow).
findings.fix: Give the post-1934-06-18 orders their own branch. For EO 6939, 6961, 6962, 7001, state the cessation condition as a TERM mechanism (ends at the IRA election if accepted; otherwise at the stated end ten years from expiry). For all eleven, replace the IRA-continuation basis with the alternatives above, and keep the lead `open` only where a statute continuing that reservation's period (named in the gaps) leaves the end undecided; otherwise lead `no`, TERM, with an interval from the election date (or order date) to the stated end.

findings.claim: These eight orders "state no expiry year and whose end no held source fixes", so they may have been running on 1934-06-18.
findings.evidence: Held later member orders for the same tribes fix or bound the ends, by the same reasoning the doctrine uses for EO 2109 and EO 4382: EO 3994 (1924-04-19) extends 'the trust period on all allotments of the Sisseton and Wahpeton Band ... for a further period of fifteen years', the same allotments EO 1916 (1914, ten years) covered (the 25 CFR ch. I appendix lists EO 1916 and then EO 3994 for Sisseton); EO 4464 extends the Papago period 'expiring during 1926 or 1927' (EO 2066, 1914, ten years); EO 4384 extends Eastern Shawnee allotments expiring in 1926 (EO 2317, 1916, ten years); EO 4407 extends the Ponca (Nebraska) allotments expiring in 1926 (EO 2374, 1916, ten years); EO 4408 extends Grande Ronde allotments 'for a further period of ten years, from present date of expiration', expiring during 1926 (EO 2376, 1916, ten years); EO 5023 extends the Iowa (Kansas and Nebraska) period expiring during 1929 (EO 2966, 1918, ten years; a weaker match). Conversely EO 3994 (1924 + 15) and EO 5383 (1930 + 10, 'from the date of expiration') cannot end before 1939 and 1940 if the period was unexpired when the order issued, so they are certainly running and belong in B07-TRUST-OPEN-CERTAIN. The branch's own gap says the lead 'would become TERM no' if a held source fixed the end before 1934-06-18.
findings.fix: Decide EO 1916, 2066, 2374, 2376 (and 2966 with a weaker-match disclosure) as `no`, TERM, with intervals ending 1924-1929 taken from the later held orders, as for EO 2109 (EO 2317 falls under R3 in any case). Move EO 3994 and 5383 to the certain branch. Correct the counts (82 + 12, 98 open, 45 no) throughout.

findings.claim: "Before 1927 such reservations were revocable at will" (Sioux Tribe v. United States, 316 U.S. 317, 331 (1942)).
findings.evidence: The quoted words are at 316 U.S. 331 (verified on justia.com: 'But the interest which the Indians received was subject to termination at the will of either the executive or Congress and without obligation to the United States'). The Court said this of the 1875-1879 Sioux orders; the 'before 1927' limit is the doctrine's inference from the 1927 Act, not the Court's holding.
findings.fix: Say that Sioux Tribe held the interest under the orders before it revocable at will, and that the 1927 Act thereafter confined boundary changes to Congress.

summary: The engine run matches the doctrine's counts (230 members, 71 decided, 6 flags, each explained). All 15 held sources have matching sha256 and their pins; the IRA, the 1935 Act, the General Allotment Act, 25 U.S.C. 5102 and 398d, Sioux Tribe, 40 CFR 49.10198(b) and the White Earth Act say what the doctrine says. The trust-period arithmetic is correct for all 45 `no` members: each order's stated expiry and period, read from the held text, gives an end before 1934-06-18. Two planted-type errors need correction: the 1906 Act is cited at 34 Stat. 352 instead of 325, and the B02-ACT-1529 date rule says 1932-08-28 although EO 5843 is dated 1932-04-28. The main legal defect is the handling of IRA sec. 2. The doctrine gives every open trust member the basis 'IRA sec. 2 continued the period the order fixed', but sec. 13 makes sec. 2 inapplicable to the listed Oklahoma tribes, which covers 19 members whose held texts show they are Oklahoma tribes. Eleven members were issued after 1934-06-18, so sec. 2 cannot have continued their periods, and four of them (EO 6939, 6961, 6962, 7001) state that they cease if the reservation accepts the IRA. Those leads stay open, so no wrong `no` or `yes` results from this, but their stated basis is false and several are decidable from their own terms. The uncertain trust branch also says no held source fixes the end of six orders whose ends are fixed by held later orders for the same tribes, the method the doctrine uses for EO 2109. The P1, P2, B02, B03, B09 and B10 branches catch the members they mean. Remaining findings are small appendix arithmetic slips and wording points.
